author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Cannot its fragrance be reproduced imaginatively?
context_before: There is nothing that appears in perception which cannot be duplicated in fancy, and what the world perceives is all imaginative in character. Here is a graphic example: I am sure everyone knows what it is to detect the fragrance of a rose. Now smell is a chemical sense and depends upon contact for perception. But does one really need a rose to detect its fragrance?
context_after: Having smelled an Easter lily, can you not discriminate between the smell of a rose and a lily, imaginatively? Then they do not exist independent of y

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: There is only one Imaginal Body.
context_before: In 1820, William Blake wrote �The Presence of the Divine Teacher,� in which he said: “Man is all Imagination and God is Man and exists in us and us in Him. The Divine Body Jesus, we are his members.” In this statement Blake does not separate the members from the one body, the one spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one God and Father of us all.
context_after: We are all His members, for we are all Imagination!

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Prayer is imagination drenched in feeling.
context_before: You can reproduce and duplicate any perception you have ever encountered, in your imagination. A friend or dear one does not need to be physically present for you to think of him. Nor do you have to be in your living room in order to see its contents. You can see the plains of Kansas, the mountains of Colorado, or the great Mississippi River without being there. So when we think from the premise of this as a world of imagination, we start on solid ground, for imagination is He who creates reality. There is no fiction in the true sense of the world, for when a state is imagined, it is created.
context_after: A desire, drenched in the feeling of fulfillment, objectifies itself. This I know to be true; so regardless of what the world thinks, when you reproduce anything in your mind it takes on form in your outer world.

quote_original: Everything here was once only imagined.
context_before: itself. This I know to be true; so regardless of what the world thinks, when you reproduce anything in your mind it takes on form in your outer world.
context_after: The clothes you wear, the chair in which you are now seated, the building which houses you – all were first only imagined. Everything begins and ends in the human imagination. The source of all phenomena is Divine Imagining, which is God Himself!

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: Then persuade yourself that the change is real.
context_before: If imagining creates reality, and you practice repentance by radically changing your mind, you can take anything that displeases you and change it.
context_after: Expect it to mold itself in harmony with what you are thinking, and the man, woman, or room, will bear witness to your repentance.

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-01-01 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: This you will know from experience.
context_before: Many believe scripture is a myth, but when it is experienced in the depth of the soul, it is literally true.
context_after: Having reached the limit of contraction to experience the nature of man, you will ascend into a limitless expansion as God.
